opening_message:
Ticket 1: Donna Ball (employee ID E024) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E024.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Donna Ball (E024) is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting write access to Source Code. Full-time employees can have up to write access; admin requires owning the system, which is not the case here. The requested write access is within policy, so recommend writer access.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB record for Donna Ball (E024) shows contractor with basic security training. Contractors can have read, or write only with advanced training. Basic training means max is read. Requested write exceeds max, so recommend read access to Source Code.
reason: The request is for write access to Source Code. The HR note lists Donna Ball (E024) as full-time, but the Security note reports that the Security DB record shows contractor status with basic security training (both facts looked up in the Security database). Under policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced security training; with basic training the maximum is read. Since the requested write exceeds the maximum, I grant the maximum of read. I rely on the Security record for the security-relevant employment/training facts, erring toward the more restrictive, policy-compliant level given the conflicting records.
